extracted.intended_audience: potential grantees, partners, donors, and policymakers seeking to align work with the Gates Foundation's priorities
extracted.subtask_description: High-level program priorities and partnership expectations that proposals or initiatives should align with when seeking funding or partnership from the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation. Covers strategic goals, geographic emphasis, tolerance for risk/innovation, and topical program areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic goals (2045)
rubrics_metrics.description: We are focused on achieving three goals by 2045: Saving the lives of mothers, babies, and children; Ending infectious diseases; Expanding economic opportunity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should align with one or more of these long-term, organization-level goals. Alignment with these goals is a primary organizing principle for the foundation's work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic presence and local partnerships ('Places')
rubrics_metrics.description: Our work depends on grantees and partners across the United States and in more than 130 countries who have on-the-ground expertise, a deep understanding of the issues we care about, and strong ties with the communities in which we aim to make a difference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The foundation values partners with local expertise and community ties. It also values having foundation representatives based in key regions to build relationships with partner organizations and governments, better understand the policy environment, and remain culturally sensitive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Willingness to fund new ideas and accept risk
rubrics_metrics.description: We support new ideas to address obstacles that stop people from living their best lives. Some projects we support will not succeed. We not only understand that, we anticipate it. Philanthropy means taking chances on solutions that governments and businesses cannot afford to take.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference for innovative or early-stage approaches that may be higher risk but have potential for outsized social impact. Applicants should expect iterative learning, and proposals should acknowledge risk and include learning/adaptation plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learning, adaptation, and sharing outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: As we discover which risks pay off, we adapt our strategies and share the outcomes for everyone's advantage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Funded work is expected to generate learnings and to be shared publicly so others can benefit; proposals should indicate how outcomes, whether positive or negative, will inform future strategy and dissemination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus on measurable results ('How we work')
rubrics_metrics.description: We are focused on results. Those that can be measured. And those measured in ways beyond numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should define clear metrics of success and be able to demonstrate measurable outcomes, while recognizing qualitative impacts too. Emphasis on evidence and measurable impact in design and evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency of grants ('Committed grants')
rubrics_metrics.description: We’ve funded thousands of projects, large and small. Our database includes payments made and committed from 1994 onward.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The foundation maintains a public record of grants and payments; applicants should expect transparency around funding and reporting, and may reference past grants in the public database.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic investments with private sector
rubrics_metrics.description: We partner with entrepreneurs, companies, and other organizations to create incentives that harness the power of private enterprise to create change for those who need it most.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supports market-based and incentive-focused strategies; proposals that leverage private-sector partnerships or create market incentives for scale and sustainability are aligned with this approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gender Equality priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Our Gender Equality Division works to ensure women and girls in Africa and South Asia can enjoy good health, make their own choices, earn their own money, and be leaders in their societies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Projects should demonstrate how they will improve health, autonomy, economic participation, or leadership opportunities for women and girls in the target geographies (particularly Africa and South Asia).

rubrics_metrics.name: Global Development priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Our Global Development Division focuses on improving the delivery of high-impact health products and services to the world’s poorest communities and helps countries expand access to health coverage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority areas include Emergency Response; Global Health Agencies and Funds; Immunization; Polio; Global Growth and Opportunity; Agricultural Development; Digital Public Infrastructure; Global Education Program; Inclusive Financial Systems; Nutrition; Water, Sanitation & Hygiene. Proposals should target delivery systems and access expansion for poor communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Global Growth & Opportunity priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Our Global Growth & Opportunity Division focuses on creating and scaling market-based innovations to stimulate inclusive and sustainable economic growth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority topics include Agricultural Development; Digital Public Infrastructure; Global Education Program; Inclusive Financial Systems; Nutrition; Water, Sanitation & Hygiene. Favor approaches that enable scaling and inclusivity through market mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Global Health priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Our Global Health Division aims to reduce inequities in health by developing new tools and strategies to reduce the burden of infectious disease and the leading causes of child mortality in developing countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program areas called out include Accelerator; Discovery & Translational Sciences; Enterics, Diagnostics, Genomics & Epidemiology (EDGE); HIV; Institute for Disease Modeling; Integrated Development; Malaria; Neglected Tropical Diseases; Pneumonia; Tuberculosis; Vaccine Development. Projects advancing new tools, diagnostics, vaccines, or strategies to reduce infectious disease and child mortality are priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Global Policy & Advocacy priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Our Global Policy & Advocacy Division seeks to build strategic relationships and promote policies that will help advance our work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work that builds strategic relationships, influences policy, or enhances partnerships is valued. Specific focus areas include Development Policy and Finance; Global Media Partnerships; Philanthropic Partnerships; Tobacco Control.

rubrics_metrics.name: U.S. Program priorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Our United States Program Division works to ensure everyone in the United States can learn, grow, and get ahead, regardless of race, gender, ethnicity, or family income.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority areas include Data; Early Learning Solutions; Economic Mobility and Opportunity; K-12 Education; Pathways; Postsecondary Success; Washington State. U.S.-focused proposals should demonstrate equity-driven impacts in education and economic mobility.
